nodes.name: Write The Hits Back To The Sheet

parameters.content:
## Re-screen your customers against OFAC, and chase the hits nobody reviewed

Sanctions lists change. A customer who was clear at onboarding may be listed next month, so
screening once is not screening. This workflow re-checks every customer in a Google Sheet against
the live OFAC list, remembers what a reviewer already cleared, and escalates any hit still sitting
unreviewed.

### How it works
Both OFAC files are downloaded first. Many parties are listed only under an alias, so if either
file fails to load the run refuses to clear anybody rather than reporting a comforting all clear.

Matching is deterministic and has no model in it: names are normalised and scored in both
directions, so one common surname does not flag everyone who shares it.

Each row is then routed one of three ways. A match a reviewer already cleared in your
reviewed-matches sheet is **suppressed**, with their name and reason, so the same false positive is
not raised every night. A new match is written back as an open hit. One open longer than your escalation window is
**escalated to Slack**, naming how many days it has been ignored.

Status, score, matched listing and first-flagged date are written back, and a digest reports what
the run found, what was suppressed and what is overdue.

### Setup
1. A Google Sheet with columns Customer Name, Customer ID, Screening Status, Screening Detail,
   Best Score, Matched Name, Screened At, First Flagged At and Cleared By. Add a second sheet with
   Customer Name, Matched Name, Cleared By and Reason.
2. Connect Google Sheets and Slack, then pick your sheets and channel.
3. Open **Screening Settings** for the threshold, recheck window and escalation window.

A score is a candidate for a human to check, never a decision.

## 1. Get the list before anything else
Both OFAC files are fetched first and retried on failure. If either one is
short or missing, no row is cleared in this run.

## 2. Read the customers
Duplicate rows collapse to one customer. Rows screened inside the recheck
window are skipped, so a nightly run only does new work.

## 3. Score every name, no model
Both directions, so a common surname does not flag everyone. Dotted
abbreviations are collapsed first, or S.A. becomes two useless tokens.

## 4. Route each row
Three ways out: suppressed by a reviewer, a new open hit, or escalated
because nobody reviewed it in time.

## 5. Say what the run found
The digest reports what this run found, not what the sheet contains.
